rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made people successors entrusted with disposal and enjoyment of the earth's resources.
rows.anchor: ملقى إليكم مقاليد التصرف والإنتفاع بما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can mean that later peoples succeeded earlier nations and inherited their worldly goods so they would give thanks through monotheism and obedience.
rows.anchor: جعلكم خلفاء ممن قبلكم من الأمم وأورثكم ما بأيديكم من متاع الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can also mean replacing nations who denied messengers and were destroyed, so people should learn from their fate.
rows.anchor: جعلكم بدل من كان قبلكم من الأمم الذين كذبوا الرسل فهلكوا

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr takes the address as general; another view restricts it to the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: والخطاب قيل عام وأستظهره في البحر وقيل : لأهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalāʾif is the regular broken plural of khalīfa; khulafāʾ is usually the plural of khalīf, though al-Wāḥidī also allows it for khalīfa.
rows.anchor: الخلائف جمع خليفة وقد أطرد جمع فعيلة على فعائل وأما الخلفاء فجمع خليف ككريم وكرماء

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī permits khulafāʾ as a plural of khalīfa, contrary to the better-known analysis.
rows.anchor: وجوز الواحدي كونه جمع خليفة أيضا وهو خلاف المشهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief means either scorning this great blessing or persisting in unbelief and abandoning faith after being guided.
rows.anchor: فمن أستمر على الكفر وترك الإيمان بعد أن لطف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consequence of disbelief falls on the disbeliever alone, not anyone else.
rows.anchor: أي وبال كفره وجزاؤه لا على غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqt means the severest contempt, hatred, and anger.
rows.anchor: أشد الإحتقار والبغض والغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The increase of loss is in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two repeated clauses explain the consequence of disbelief; repetition reinforces the warning because divine abhorrence and loss each independently establish its ugliness.
rows.anchor: والتكرير لزيادة التقرير والتنبيه على أن إقتضاء الكفر لكل واحد واحد من الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whomever God grants a long life is reversed in bodily development, with steadily increasing weakness and loss of structure and powers.
rows.anchor: نقلبه فيه فلا يزال يتزايد ضعفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image transfers physical reversal to the person's condition by analogy: aging runs opposite to the beginning of life.
rows.anchor: وفيه تشبيه التنكيس المعنوي بالتنكيس الحسي واستعارة الحسي له

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyān says this reversal begins at age eighty.
rows.anchor: وعن سفيان أن التنكيس في سن ثمانين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects a fixed age of eighty: the onset of weakness varies with temperaments and circumstances.
rows.anchor: والحق أن زمان ابتداء الضعف وانتقاص البنية مختلف لاختلاف الأمزجة والعوارض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause coordinates with the earlier wish to erase sight as a cause-effect pairing, and serves as evidence for that power.
rows.anchor: عطف العلة على المعلول لأنه كالشاهد لذلك

rows.speaker: جمع من السبعة
rows.claim: A group of the Seven read nunakkisuhu with a light form, from ankasa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمع من السبعة ( ننكسه ) مخففا من الإنكاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether people see this and still fail to infer that the One who can do it can also erase or transform them; those acts are absent only because God does not will them.
rows.anchor: أيرون ذلك فلا يعقلون أن من قدر على ذلك يقدر على ما ذكر من الطمس والمسخ

rows.speaker: نافع، ابن ذكوان، أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Dhakwān, and Abū ʿAmr in the ʿAyyāsh transmission read taʿqilūn, second-person address, matching the preceding address.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن ذكوان وأبو عمرو في رواية عياش ( تعقلون ) بتاء الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation in truth establishes the unity and sovereign power already mentioned; the world is made with wisdom and benefits.
rows.anchor: إثبات لما ذكر أولا من الوحدة والقهر وفيه أيضا ما ستعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses about night and day explain how God governs the created world, whose alternation depends on celestial bodies moving.
rows.anchor: بيان لكيفية تصرفه فيما ذكر بعد بيان الخلق فإن حدوث الليل والنهار منوط بتحريك أجرام سماوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takwīr originally means wrapping or winding, as one winds a turban around the head.
rows.anchor: والتكوير في الأصل هو اللف واللي من كار العمامة على رأسه وكورها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda explains the verse as one of night and day covering the other.
rows.anchor: والمراد على ما روي عن قتادة يغشى أحدهما الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the covering interpretation, one withdraws and the other covers its place, turning it dark or bright; the place may be the literal thing covered or the two periods may be personified.
rows.anchor: يذهب أحدهما ويغشى مكانه الآخر أي يلبسه مكانه فيصير أسود مظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation compares one period's disappearance when the other arrives to an object wrapped over something and hidden from sight.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد واحد من الليل والنهار يغيب الآخر إذا طرأ عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading is their repeated successive circling, like layers of a turban; it is called strongest because it combines wrapping and recurrence.
rows.anchor: قيل وهو الأرجح لأنه اعتبر فيه ما اعتبر مع الأول مع النظر إلى المطرد فيه لفظ الكور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in reports from al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Abī Ḥātim, explains one period as carrying the other by adding portions, lengthening one and shortening the other.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن المعنى يحمل أحدهما على الآخر وفسر هذا الحمل بالضم والزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense of carrying one into the other is clear and resembles the verse saying God inserts night into day and day into night.
rows.anchor: يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covering sense echoes the description of night and day as succeeding one another for remembrance.
rows.anchor: جعل الليل والنهار خلفة لمن أراد أن يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addition sense echoes the oath by the night that covers and the day that shines.
rows.anchor: والليل إذا يغشى والنهار إذا تجلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successive-pursuit sense echoes the description of night covering day in rapid pursuit; several kinds of metaphor or simile are possible, with representation the best fit.
rows.anchor: يغشي الليل النهار يطلبه حثيثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb indicates continuing renewal.
rows.anchor: وأيا ما كان فصيغة المضارع للدلالة على التجدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subjected the sun and moon and made them obedient to His command.
rows.anchor: جعلهما منقادين لأمره عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each luminary runs until its orbital cycle ends or its motion ceases.
rows.anchor: كل منهما يجري لمنتهى دورته أو منقطع حركته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse proves that the sun moves; al-Ālūsī criticizes claims that it is stationary and the world's center, including a recent European claim that it moves around another center.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن الشمس متحركة وزعم بعض الكفرة أنها ساكنة وأنها مركز العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is the One able to punish those who persist in unbelief.
rows.anchor: ألا هو العزيز ( القادر على عقاب المصرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghaffār forgives the sins of those who repent.
rows.anchor: لذنوب التائبين أو الغالب الذي يقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation calls God conquering and able to punish, yet describes His postponement of punishment as forgiveness by a metaphor based on their shared feature of withholding.
rows.anchor: الغالب الذي يقدر أن يعالجهم بالعقوبة وهو سبحانه يحلم عليهم ويؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor of forgiveness for withholding punishment is stronger and better than the proposed metonymy.
rows.anchor: وجوز كون ذلك من باب المجاز المرسل والأول أبلغ وأحسن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī gives both explanations of al-ʿAzīz al-Ghaffār: actual forgiveness of repentant sinners or power restrained through forbearance.
rows.anchor: الوجهان في ( العزيز الغفار ) قد ذكرهما الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that the first reading should be abandoned as Muʿtazilite; God may forgive others too, while mentioning repentance best fits the context.
rows.anchor: وما علينا أن نفسر كما فسر ونقول بأن مغفرته تعالى لا تخص التائبين بل قد يغفر جل شأنه لغيرهم

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says the first explanation suits creation in truth: perfect power and mercy warrant punishment for obstinacy and forgiveness for repentance.
rows.anchor: ما فيه من الدلالة على كمال القدرة وكمال الرحمة المقتضى لعقاب المصر وغفران ذنوب التائب

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf also links the first explanation to the passage's rejection of shirk: creation and revelation establish worship and sincere devotion, and the ending encourages seeking forgiveness while warning of disbelief and sin.
rows.anchor: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق والحكمة التي منها الجزاء على ما سلف فالتذييل بإلا هو العزيز الغفار للترغيب في طلب المغفرة

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī prefers the second contextual correspondence, in which the ending intensifies condemnation of the shirk and divine offspring attributed to God.
rows.anchor: وقد آثر هذا العلامة الطيبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds the first explanation's broader fit stronger; the chapter centers on worship, sincerity, and warning against unbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: ويعلم مما ذكرنا وجه رجحان الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship whatever they wish conveys intense anger: since they would not stop, they are told to proceed so punishment can come upon them.
rows.anchor: وفيه من الدلالة على شدة الغضب عليهم ما لا يخفى كأنهم لما لم ينتهوا عما نهوا عنه أمروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The losers are those fully ruined, having squandered themselves and what they needed to secure.
rows.anchor: أي الكاملين في الخسران وهو إضاعة ما بهم وإترافهم ما لا بد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the main interpretation, their families are followers whom they misled; they ruin themselves and those followers by choosing unbelief.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالأهل أتباعهم الذين أضلوهم أي أضاعوا أنفسهم وأضاعوا أهليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The loss occurs when they enter Hell, having exposed themselves and their followers to everlasting torment.
rows.anchor: حين يدخلون النار حيث عرضوهما للعذاب السرمدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the Day of Resurrection as the point when their loss becomes manifest and is fully realized.
rows.anchor: ولو أبقى يوم القيامة على ظاهره لأنه يتبين فيه أمرهم ويتحقق مبدأ خسرانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view takes family as followers generally: if they are in Hell, the losers lose themselves; if in Paradise, they are irretrievably separated from them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالأهل الأتباع مطلقا وخسرانهم إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that separation from the Paradise-bound would be no meaningful loss if reunion would bring no benefit to the loser.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأن المحذور ذهاب من لو آب لا ينتفع به الخاسر وذلك غير متصور في الشق الأخير

rows.speaker: قتادة، مجاهد، ميمون بن مهران
rows.claim: Qatāda, Mujāhid, and Maymūn ibn Mihrān say everyone has a family prepared in Paradise if they obey God; unbelievers lose that family.
rows.anchor: ليس أحد إلا قد أعد الله تعالى له أهلا في الجنة إن أطاعه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they lose the Paradise-dwellers prepared for them had they obeyed God, thereby depriving those companions too.
rows.anchor: خسروا أهليهم من أهل الجنة كانوا أعدوا لهم لو عملوا بطاعة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains the family as the houris; al-Ālūsī says this reading is somewhat remote.
rows.anchor: فقد روي عنه أنه فسر الأهل بالحور العين ولا يخفى أن حمل الآية على ذلك لا يخلو عن بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement does more than define complete losers: it identifies them as those addressed by the preceding command, either directly or as the foremost members of its category.
rows.anchor: بل بيان أنهم المخاطبون بما تقدم إما بجعل الموصول عبارة عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding sentence is independent; its demonstrative marks the loss as remote and immense, while the emphatic pronoun, definite noun, intensive form, and mubīn underscore its totality and horror.
rows.anchor: وتصديرها بحرف التنبيه والإشارة بذلك إلى بعد منزلة المشار إليه في النشر وأنه لعظمه بمنزلة المحسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form khusrān is more emphatic than khusr, and describing it as manifest leaves no greater kind of loss beyond it.
rows.anchor: وتعريف الخسران والإتيان به على فعلان الأبلغ من فعل ووصفه بالمبين من الدلالة على كمال هو له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the stories are given for consolation, the Prophet is told to endure the harm inflicted by the polytheists.
rows.anchor: إذا عرفت ما قصصناه عليك للتأسي فاصبر على ما نالك من أذية المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise to the Prophet and believers is victory, explicitly linked to the promise in 40:51; alternatively it includes all divine promises, especially victory.
rows.anchor: النصر المشار إليه بقوله سبحانه : ( إنا لننصر رسلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God never breaks His promise, so victory for the Prophet and believers must occur; the fates of Moses and Pharaoh provide an example.
rows.anchor: لا يخلفه سبحانه أصلا فلا بد من وقوع نصره جل شأنه لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness means turning diligently to religious duties and repairing lapses that count as sins relative to the Prophet's rank, though not actual sins.
rows.anchor: أقبل علي أمر الدين وتلاف ما ربما يفرط مما يعد بالنسبة إليك ذنبا وإن لم يكنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the sin as the community's sin against the Prophet, with the genitive construction understood as an objective relation.
rows.anchor: لذنبك ) لذنب أمتك في حقك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning evening and morning may mean persistence in glorification and praise throughout all times.
rows.anchor: عبر بالطرفين وأريد جميع الأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command can mean the two specified periods, with glorification in its literal sense or as prayer.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد خصوص الوقتين والمراد بالتسبيح معناه الحقيقي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets the two periods as the dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : أريد صلاة الغداة وصلاة العصر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets them as two rakʿahs in the morning and two in the evening; the source discusses differing claims about what was obligatory in Mecca.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أريد ركعتان بكرة وركعتان عشيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās takes the command as the five daily prayers when glorification means prayer.
rows.anchor: وحكى ذلك في البحر عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who dispute God's signs include those disputing His proofs of unity, revealed books, and miracles without a God-given proof; religious argument must rest on clear evidence.
rows.anchor: دلائله سبحانه التي نصبها على توحيده وكتبه المنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule applies to every false disputant, although the immediate occasion was, most likely, Meccan polytheists.
rows.anchor: وهذا عام في كل مجادل مبطل وإن نزل في قوم مخصوصين وهم على الأصح مشركو مكة

none: bare connective introducing a quotation; no exegetical point

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Respond to the Lord when the Messenger calls you to what brings salvation.
rows.anchor: إذا دعاكم لما به النجاة على لسان رسوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن ملك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik allows min Allāh to attach to mard, treating the la-noun like a quasi-annexed noun and leaving it without tanwīn; the source adduces two parallels.
rows.anchor: الجار والمجرور إمامتعلق بمرد ويعامل اسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse supplies an omitted demonstrative subject: the day is from God, as an independent answer to the question, from whom?
rows.anchor: هو خبر لمبتدأ محذوف أي ذلك من الله تعالى والجملة استئناف في جواب سؤال مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammarians make the phrase circumstantial, attach it to the negation, or connect it to what the wording implies, comparing 68:2.
rows.anchor: أو حال من الضمير المستتر في الظرف الواقع خبر لا أو متعلق بالنفي أو بما دل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching the phrase to yaʾtī is contrary to the apparent wording and sense; describing the day with it is also weak in meaning.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو متعلق بيأتي وتعقب أنه خلاف المتبادر من اللفظ والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent referent of the irreversible day is the Resurrection, rather than the day of death.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بذلك اليوم يوم القيامة لا يوم ورود الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maljaʾ can be a place noun meaning refuge or a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: اسم مكان ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا ميميا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nakir means denial as a verbal noun, irregularly formed; their denial that they were idolaters is treated as nothing because it cannot help against evidence and testimony of their limbs.
rows.anchor: إنكار على أنه مصدر أنكر على غير القياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says there is no denial because circumstances and stations differ, so what they say in one state does not count as denial in another.
rows.anchor: أو يقال أن الأمرين باعتبار تعدد الأحوال والمواقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible active-participle sense is that no one distinguishes their conditions in order to show mercy, but al-Ālūsī calls this far-fetched.
rows.anchor: أن يكون ( نكير ) اسم فاعل للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening reports the outcome of their misguidance, sealing of hearing and hearts, and covering of sight; the pronoun can refer to the unbelievers or their state.
rows.anchor: بيان لأحكام إضلالهم والختم على سمعهم وقلوبهم وجعل غشاوة على أبصارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in mā hiya may mean life itself or the worldly state; either way the exception is from the same category.
rows.anchor: ما هي أي ما الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their statement generalizes about humankind: one group dies and another lives, with no resurrection; the order is chosen for the verse ending.
rows.anchor: حكم على النوع بجملته من غير اعتبار تقديم وتأخير إلا أن تأخير نحيي في النظم الجليل للفاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate word order, “we live and die,” has been proposed, but al-Ālūsī says it is not convincing.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في الكلام تقديم وتأخير أي نحيا ونموت وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes death as the pre-ensoulment state before life begins.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أرادوا بالموت عدمك الحياة السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading uses life figuratively for the continuing descendants after their own deaths.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أرادوا بالحياة بقاء النسل والذرية مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility assigns death and life to different people by figurative attribution.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أرادوا يموت بعضنا ويحيا بعض على التجوز في الإسناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading life as reincarnation into another body reflects a belief of many idolaters, but al-Ālūsī says it is unlikely here.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يريدوا بالحياة على سبيل المجاز إعادة الروح لبدن آخر بطريق التناسخ وهو اعتقاد كثير من عبدة الأصنام ولا يخفى بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dahr means a long stretch of time and is narrower than zamān according to al-Saʿd; al-Rāghib describes it as the world's duration or any long period.
rows.anchor: فالدهر أخص من الزمان وهو الذي ارتضاه السعد

rows.speaker: الراغب، الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says dahr originally names the world's whole duration and then any long period; al-Khalīl records a use meaning that an affliction befell someone for a long time.
rows.anchor: ثم يعبر به عن كل مدة كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blaming time for destruction denies the Angel of Death and attributes events to time through ignorance that God decrees them.
rows.anchor: وإسنادهم الإهلاك إلى الدهر إنكار منهم لملك الموت وقبضه الأرواح بأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These speakers acknowledge God, unlike outright materialist Dahriyya, though both groups treat time as an independent cause; philosophers often measure time by celestial motion.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء معترفون وجود الله تعالى فهم غير الدهرية فإنهم مع إسنادهم الحوادث إلى الدهر لا يقولون بوجوده سبحانه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Muslim reports the prohibition on cursing time and the warning that God is the one who turns night and day.
rows.anchor: لا يسب أحدكم الدهر فإن اللههو الدهر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Reports in Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, al-Ḥākim, and al-Bayhaqī prohibit cursing time; the cited divine speech says God turns night and day and brings events, so cursing time as agent falls on God.
rows.anchor: معنى ذلك أن الله تعالى هو الآتي بالحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars count cursing time as a major sin because it can lead to cursing God; al-Ālūsī notes that Shāfiʿī legal language calls it disliked rather than forbidden or major.
rows.anchor: وعد بعضهم سبه كبيرة لأنه يؤدي إلى سبه تعالى وهو كفر

rows.speaker: الشافعية
rows.claim: The Shāfiʿī position is explicit that cursing time is disliked, not forbidden or a major sin.
rows.anchor: وكلام الشافعية صريح بأن ذلك مكروه ولا حرام فضلا عن كونه كبيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī distinguishes meanings: cursing time itself is disliked; intending God or the true efficient cause is unbelief; an unqualified curse is ambiguous, though time is the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: فلا كلام في الكلاهة أوالله عز وجل فلا كلام في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that time-cursing is major when one believes time has causal power misses that this belief itself is unbelief, not merely a ruling about the curse.
rows.anchor: إن سبه كبيرة إن اعتقد أن له تأثيرا فيما نزل به كما كان يعتقد جهلة العرب وفيه نظر لأن اعتقاد ذلك كفر

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most scholars retain the nominative reading in the report “I am time”; it does not make time a divine name because the wording is figurative.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم كان الجمهور على ضم الراء ولا يلزم عليه أن يكون من أسمائه تعالى لما سبق أن ذلك على التجوز

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some reject the nominative reading of the Abū Dāwūd and Ḥākim report as implying a divine name, and instead read time as an accusative adverb of duration.
rows.anchor: وأنكر بعضهم كون ما في حديث أبي داود والحاكم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib proposes that the second dahr in Muslim's report is a verbal noun meaning the active manager who directs events; al-Ālūsī considers this unlikely.
rows.anchor: الراغب عن بعضهم أن الدهر الثاني في حديث مسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads “except time passes,” interpreting dahr as the time that elapses.
rows.anchor: إلا دهر ) وتأويله إلا دهر يمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their assertion lacks rational or transmitted evidence and rests only on conjecture and imitation.
rows.anchor: ما هم إلا قوم قصارى أمرهم الظن والتقليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial faʾ can answer an implicit condition: given the unbelievers' fate, or God's demonstrated power, endure what they inflict.
rows.anchor: إذا كان عاقبة أمر الكفرة ما ذكر فاصبر على ما يصيبك من جهتهم

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr treats the faʾ as joining this sentence to earlier reports about the afterlife: their state is thus, so do not hurry and fear only God.
rows.anchor: واقتصر في البحر على كونها لعطف هذه الجملة على أخبار في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A number of commentators instead take the faʾ as joining this sentence to the preceding passage, with a clear causal force.
rows.anchor: وجوز غير واحد كونها عاطفة لهذه الجملة على ما تقدم والسببية فيها ظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm can mean firm resolve and exertion in an affair, or patience in it.
rows.anchor: والعزم يطلق على الجد والاجتهاد في الشيء وعلى الصبر عليه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد، الجبائي، جماعة
rows.claim: On the explanatory reading of min, all messengers are possessors of resolve: they persist in conveying revelation and patiently accept God's commands and decrees.
rows.anchor: إليه ذهب ابن زيد والجبائي وجماعة أي

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني، الحسن بن الفضل، الكلبي، مقاتل، قتادة، أبو العالية، ابن جريج
rows.claim: Most exegetes take min as partitive, meaning that only some messengers are the possessors of resolve; they differ over who and how many.
rows.anchor: وعن عطاء الخراساني والحسن بن الفضل والكلبي ومقاتل وقتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Faḍl counts eighteen, identified with the prophets named in al-Anʿām, followed by the command to follow their guidance.
rows.anchor: ثمانية عشر وهم المذكورون في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One unnamed view counts nine: Noah, Abraham, the son intended for sacrifice, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Moses, David, and Jesus, each noted for a trial endured.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تسعة نوح عليه السلام صبر على أذى قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another unnamed view counts seven: Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, David, Solomon, and Jesus.
rows.anchor: وقيل : سبعة آدم ونوح وإبراهيم وموسى وداود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās counts six messengers commanded to fight: Noah, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Moses, David, and Solomon.
rows.anchor: وأخرجه ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس وعن مقاتل أنهم ستة ولم يذكر حديث الأمر بالقتال

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil's six are Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, and Job.
rows.anchor: وقال : هم نوح وإبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A report from Qatāda counts five: Noah, Hūd, Abraham, Shuʿayb, and Moses.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن عساكر عن قتادة أنهم نوح وهود وإبراهيم وشعب وموسى عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Another report from Qatāda counts four: Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus; al-Ālūsī calls this the soundest view.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عنه أنهم نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى وظاهره القول بأنهم أربعة وهذا أصح الأقوال

rows.speaker: السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyūṭī calls the five-person view soundest: those four plus Muḥammad, citing a report from Ibn ʿAbbās and authorities of the Prophet's household.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الأربعة ونبينا صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the five are not the verse's intended list, since the command would then ask the Prophet to imitate his own patience.
rows.anchor: إذ يلزم عليه أمره عليه الصلاة والسلام أن يصبر كصبر نفسه ولا يكاد يصح ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: A report attributed to Abū al-ʿĀliya counts Noah, Abraham, Hūd, and the Messenger as a fourth.
rows.anchor: قول أبي العالية فيما أخرجه عبد بن حميد وأبو الشيخ والبيهقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī favors the explanatory reading, urging patience as the messengers generally endured; the term later commonly denotes the famous five.
rows.anchor: ولعل الأولى في الآبة القول الأول وإن صار أولوا العزم بعد مختصا بأولئك الخمسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not ask for the punishment of Meccan unbelievers to be hastened; it is near to falling upon them.
rows.anchor: أي لكفار مكة بالعذاب أي لا تدع بتعجيله فإنه على شرف النزول بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they see the promised punishment, its severity makes their time in the world seem no longer than a brief hour of a day.
rows.anchor: لما يشاهدون من شدة العذاب وطوا مدته

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads “from the day” with the definite article.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( من النهار )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balāgh can be an omitted-subject predicate meaning that the admonition suffices, or mean a communication by the Messenger; the reference might be the Qurʾān or the sūra.
rows.anchor: بلاغ خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هذا الذي وعظتم به كفاية في الموعظة أو تبليغ من الرسول

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز، أبو سراج الهذلي
rows.claim: Abū Majlaz and Abū Sirāj al-Hudhalī read balagh as an imperative, “convey,” supporting the communication interpretation.
rows.anchor: بقراءة أبي مجلز وأبي سراج الهذلي ( بلغ ) بصيغة الأمر

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: In another transmission Abū Majlaz reads ballagha in the past tense; Abū Ḥayyān instead favors the brief sojourn as the referent of balāgh, like “brief enjoyment.”
rows.anchor: وبقراءة أبي مجلز أيضا في رواية ( بلغ ) بصيغة الماضي من التفعيل

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: Abū Majlaz also parses balāgh as a nominative subject whose predicate is the earlier lahum; al-Ālūsī calls this very weak because it interrupts the apparent syntax.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مجلز : ( بلاغ ) مبتدأ خبره قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحسن، زيد بن علي، عيسى
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and ʿĪsā read accusative balāghan, with an implied verb such as “convey a communication.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وزيد بن علي وعيسى ( بلاغا ) بالنصب بتقدير بلغ بلاغا

rows.speaker: الحسن، زيد بن علي، عيسى
rows.claim: These readers also transmit a genitive reading, making balāgh an adjective for “day.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ أيضا ( بلاغ ) بالجر على أنه نعت لنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The last clause warns that only those who leave admonition or obedience are destroyed.
rows.anchor: الخارجون عن الاتعاظ أو عن الطاعة وفي الآية من الوعيد والإنذار

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin is reported by Ibn Khālawayh with two forms of the verb yahlik; Abū al-Fatḥ calls the form with kasra in the past rare and disfavored.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن فيما حكى عنه ابن خالويه ( يهلك ) بفتح الياء وكسر اللام

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Thābit reads nahlik with the majestic first-person plural and puts “the sinful people” in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن ثابت ( نهلك ) بنون العظمة من الإهلاك ( القوم الفاسقين ) بالنصب

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī in al-Duʿāʾ transmits from Anas, from the Prophet, a supplication for a need to be fulfilled that includes these verses and asks for mercy, forgiveness, relief, payment of debts, and every worldly and otherworldly need.
rows.anchor: أخرج الطبراني في الدعاء عن أنس عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : إذا طلبت حاجة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports that ʿAlī said Sūrat Muḥammad was revealed concerning Banū Umayya.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه قال : نزلت سورة محمد آية في بني أمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī doubts that the report about Banū Umayya is sound.
rows.anchor: ولا أظن صحة الخبر نعم لكفار بني أمية الحظ الأوفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Banū Umayya fall under the Qurʾān's general descriptions of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: لكفار بني أمية الحظ الأوفر من عمومات الآيات التي في الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, the Prophet's household fall under the general descriptions of believers.
rows.anchor: كما أن لأهل البيت رضي الله تعالى عنهم المعلى والرقيب من عمومات الآيات التي في المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī condemns whoever severs family ties and harms the Prophet's household.
rows.anchor: لعن الله تعالى من قطع الأرحام وآذى الآل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says no more should be said beyond this general inclusion, except to condemn harm to the Prophet's household.
rows.anchor: وأكثر من هذا لا يقال سوى أني أقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be patient with polytheists' denials of resurrection: the One who created the world rapidly can resurrect and punish them.
rows.anchor: ما يقول المشركون في شأن البعث من الأباطيل المبنية على الاستبعاد والإنكار فإن من قدر على خلق العالم في تلك المدة اليسيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, endure the Jews' blasphemous and anthropomorphic claims.
rows.anchor: أو على ما يقول اليهود من مقالة الكفر والتشبيه

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says the first reading connects the command to the sūra's opening through this point, fitting the continuous argument better than attaching it only to the immediately preceding creation statement.
rows.anchor: على الأول متعلق بأول السورة إلى هذا الموضع وأنه أنسب من تعلقه بلقد خلقنا الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī considers the nearer connection to be with the preceding creation statement on either interpretation.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن الأقرب تعلقه على الوجهين بما ذكرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorify God as free of incapacity and of breaking His promise of resurrection, and of any likeness to creation; it can also mean all imperfections while praising Him for guidance and other favors.
rows.anchor: نزهه تعالى عن العجز عما يمكن وعن وقوع الخلف في أخباره التي من جملتها الأخبار بوقوع البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sunrise and sunset denote the times of the Fajr and ʿAṣr prayers, whose virtue is well known.
rows.anchor: هما وقتا الفجر والعصر وفضيلتهما مشهورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed lā may be an emphatic extra particle, as in the Qurʾānic example lā-yaʿlama ahlu al-kitāb.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : ( لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب )

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān chooses to treat lā as an oath-lām whose vowel is lengthened into an alif, adducing a rare analogous spelling and a Qurʾānic reading.
rows.anchor: أو هي لام القسم أشبعت فتحتها فتولدت منها ألف نظير ما

rows.speaker: الحسن، عيسى
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read falā qasam, supporting the analysis that the following clause is a present-tense oath.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد قراءة الحسن وعيسى فلا قسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This analysis assumes a present-tense verb can be sworn by; the cited grammarians permit that, whereas Ibn ʿAṣfūr and the Basrans say a present verb takes an oath only when intended as future and then requires the emphatic nūn.
rows.anchor: فعل الحال يجوز القسم عليه فيقال

rows.speaker: ابن عصفور، البصريون
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṣfūr and Basran grammarians reject swearing by a present-tense verb; when future meaning is intended they require emphatic nūn, making its omission very weak.
rows.anchor: والذي اختاره ابن عصفور والبصريون

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān parses the readings with an omitted subject and initial lām, roughly “for I indeed swear,” though the author objects that omitting the emphasized subject is awkward.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا خرجوا قراءة الحسن وعيسى على أن اللام لام الابتداء والمبتدأ محذوف لأنها لا تدخل على الفعل

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وبعض النحاة
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and some grammarians take lā as denying unbelievers' claims that the Qurʾān is sorcery, poetry, or soothsaying, then begin a new oath.
rows.anchor: لا نفي ورد لما يقوله الكفار في القرآن من أنه سحر وشعر وكهانة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects to the denial reading because it requires deleting both the subject and predicate of lā outside a question-answer construction.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه أبو حيان بأنه لا يجوز لما فيه من حذف اسم لا وخبرها في غير جواب سؤال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view treats lā before an oath as an opening formula, as in the cited line addressed to Ibnat al-ʿĀmirī.
rows.anchor: إن لا كثيرا ما يؤتى بها قبل القسم على نحو الاستفتاح

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم وجمع
rows.claim: Abū Muslim and others take the words literally: no oath is needed because the matter is too clear, much less this great oath; al-Ālūsī rejects the Rūmī muftī's objection as inattentive.
rows.anchor: إن الكلام على ظاهره المتبادر منه والمعنى لا أقسم إذ الأمر أوضح من أن يحتاج إلى قسم

rows.speaker: قتادة، الحسن
rows.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan take the sites of the stars as their settings, since their disappearance points to an enduring, unchanging Agent and the time is associated with worship and mercy.
rows.anchor: بمساقط كواكب السماء ومغاربها كما جاء في رواية عن قتادة والحسن

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit a raised report from Abū Hurayra that God descends in the last third of the night and calls people to pray, ask, and seek forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ينزل ربنا كل ليلة إلى سماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A second report from al-Ḥasan takes the sites as the stars' scattering on the Resurrection; their fall need not occur all at once and displays divine majesty while confirming resurrection.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أيضا المراد مواقعها عند الانكدار يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر، أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbd Allāh, from their forefathers, identify the sites as where stars fall after jinn eavesdroppers are pursued.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله على آبائهما وعليهما السلام المراد مواقعها عند الانقضاض إثر المسترقين السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view means the lunar mansions that pre-Islamic Arabs believed caused rain; the occasion report is not decisive, since ordinary settings could also be intended.
rows.anchor: وقيل : مواقع النجوم هي الأنواء التي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda, in reports from ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Jarīr, says the sites are the stars' stations and paths, with “falling” meaning descent, a sign of God's immense power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وابن جرير عن قتادة أنها منازلها ومجاريها على أن الوقوع النزول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say the sites are the occasions of Qurʾānic revelation; reports say it descended all at once to the lowest heaven, then in installments over years.
rows.anchor: وقال جماعة منهم ابن عباس : النجوم نجوى القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Jarīr, al-Ḥākim (who authenticates it), and al-Bayhaqī transmit Ibn ʿAbbās's account of the Qurʾān's descent in one night and later installments.
rows.anchor: أنزل القرآن في ليلة من السماء العليا إلى السماء الدنيا جملة واحدة ثم فرق السنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation reading gives the next verse's pronoun an evident antecedent and needs no contextual inference; its rationale is especially clear.
rows.anchor: وأيد هذا القول بأن الضمير في قوله تعالى بعد : ( إنه لقرآن ) يعود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، أهل المدينة، حمزة، الكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, the Medinans, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read the singular mawqiʿ, intended collectively.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وأهل المدينة وحمزة والكسائي ( بموقع ) مفردا مرادا به الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence “it is a tremendous oath” is an interjection within another parenthesis, interrupting the oath before its sworn subject.
rows.anchor: مشتمل على اعتراض في ضمن آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is play with no fruit beyond toil, distraction from serious concerns, adornment without intrinsic honor, boasting in ancestry, and competing in numbers, wealth, and children.
rows.anchor: بأنها لعب لا ثمرة فيها سوى التعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adornment means fine clothes, handsome mounts, and lofty homes, which give no inherent distinction.
rows.anchor: لا يحصل منها شرف ذاتي كالملابس الحسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boasting is over old ancestors, while accumulation concerns numbers and possessions.
rows.anchor: بالأنساب والعظام البالية ( وتكاثر ) بالعدد والعدد

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī reads tafākhur baynikum with genitive construction.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي ( وتفاخر بينكم ) بالإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain-growth comparison shows how quickly worldly beauty fades; the next part warns of severe punishment or immense forgiveness and favor in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ثم يكون حطاما ( هشيما متكسرا من اليبس

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd explains the “kuffār” who admire the crop as farmers, since they cover seeds in the earth.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالكفار إما الحراث على ما روي عن ابن مسعود لأنهم يكفرون أي يسترون البذور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, kuffār means unbelievers, who are more captivated by worldly decoration; a believer transfers wonder from what is seen to its Creator.
rows.anchor: وأما الكافرون بالله سبحانه ووجه تخصيصهم أنهم أشد إعجابا بزينة الدنيا

rows.speaker: أبو نواس
rows.claim: Abū Nuwās's narcissus poem pictures silver eyes and gold on emerald stems as witnesses that God has no partner, illustrating how beauty points beyond itself.
rows.anchor: قال أبو نواس في النرجس : عيون من لجين شاخصات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A disbeliever, by contrast, does not move thought beyond sensory experience and is wholly absorbed in admiration.
rows.anchor: والكافر لا يتخطى فكره عما أحس به فيستغرق إعجابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahīj can mean the plant reaches its utmost growth or, alternatively, dries after being green and fresh.
rows.anchor: يهيج ( يتحرك إلى أقصى ما يتأتى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant then appears yellow after having looked fresh; one reading is muṣfārran, and the shift from “it yellows” may signal that yellowing is not simultaneous with maturation or is obvious to all.
rows.anchor: بعد ما رأيته ناضرا مونقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun kāf may be accusative as a circumstantial phrase linked to “play,” or nominative as a second predicate with an omitted “likeness of life.”
rows.anchor: قيل : النصب على الحالية من الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant's short cycle compresses the many years of worldly life into less than a year, showing how quickly it disappears.
rows.anchor: ولتضمن ذلك تشبيه جميع ما فيها من السنين الكثيرة بمدة نبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After worldly life is disparaged, the afterlife is magnified to encourage lasting bliss and warn against painful punishment; punishment is mentioned first as a consequence of immersion in worldly pursuits.
rows.anchor: وبعد ما بين حقارة أمر الدنيا تزهيدا فيها وتنفيرا عن العكوف عليها أشير إلى فخامة شأن الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pairing forgiveness and favor against one punishment signals mercy's predominance, like the saying that one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: وفي مقابلة العذاب الشديد بشيئين إشارة إلى غلبة الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not describing punishment as “from God” while explicitly attaching forgiveness and favor to God further signals mercy's predominance and that good is the primary aim.
rows.anchor: وفي ترك وصف العذاب بكونه من الله تعالى مع وصف ما بعده بذلك إشارة إلى غلبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is delusive enjoyment for someone who rests in it instead of using it as a means to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لمن اطمأن بها ولم يجعلها ذريعة للآخرة ومطية لنعيمها

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the world is delusive enjoyment if it distracts from the afterlife, but an excellent provision and means when it leads to God's pleasure and the next life.
rows.anchor: الدنيا متاع الغرور إن ألهتك عن طلب الآخرة فأما إذا دعتك إلى طلب رضوان الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā covers everything one does and leaves undone.
rows.anchor: في كل ما تأتون وتذرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tomorrow” means Resurrection because it is near as tomorrow is to yesterday, or because worldly life is like a day before the distinct conditions of the next life; its indefiniteness magnifies an unknowable, tremendous day.
rows.anchor: عبر عنه بذلك لدنوه دنو الغد من أمسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite nafs minimizes the number who truly examine their deeds, strengthening the exhortation and censuring widespread heedlessness.
rows.anchor: وأما تنكير ( نفس ) فلاستقلال الأنفس النواظر

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says the command to examine is broad, but those who actually comply are exceedingly few; it cites a report comparing people to a hundred camels with scarcely one fit mount.
rows.anchor: لأن الأمر بالنظر وإن عم لكن المؤتمر الناظر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya suggests that “tomorrow” means the day after death; al-Ālūsī says this is weak.
rows.anchor: وجوز ابن عطية أن يراد بعد يوم الموت وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة، يحيى بن الحارث، حفص
rows.claim: Abū Ḥaywa, Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥārith, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read li-tanẓur with a kasra on the lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة ويحيى بن الحرث

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the lām with kasra and the rāʾ with fatḥa as a purpose particle, yielding “so that a soul may consider.”
rows.anchor: لام كي وكان المعنى ولكن تنظر نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to fear God may emphasize the first command, or distinguish fulfilling obligations from avoiding prohibitions.
rows.anchor: واتقوا الله ( تكرير للتأكيد أو الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī initially favors the distinction: the first taqwā concerns required actions and the second avoiding forbidden acts, with the warning supporting the latter.
rows.anchor: في ترك المحارم كما يؤذن به الوعيد بقوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says taqwā already includes avoiding sin, so there is no basis to divide the two commands and emphasis better fits the passage; al-Ālūsī objects that the preceding phrase naturally suggests good deeds and finally leans toward distinction.
rows.anchor: ولاوجه وجيه للتوزيع والمقام مقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not let attention to managing, benefiting from, and enjoying wealth and children distract from prayer and other acts that recall the true object of worship.
rows.anchor: لا يشغلكم الاهتمام بتدبير أمورها والاعتناء بمصالحها والتمتع بها عن الاشتغال بذكر الله عز وجل من الصلاة وسائر العبادات

rows.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and others take remembrance of God as a metonym for all worship, since worship causes remembrance and remembrance is its true aim.
rows.anchor: فذكر الله تعالى مجاز عن مطلق العبادة كما يقتضيه كلام الحسن وجماعة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A report from al-Ḥasan takes remembrance to mean all obligatory duties.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن الحسن أن المراد به جميع الفرائض

rows.speaker: الضحاك، عطاء
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿAṭāʾ say remembrance here means the obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك وعطاء : الذكر هنا الصلاة المكتوبة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī interprets remembrance as fighting alongside the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : الجهاد مع الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the general interpretation of remembrance as worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل : القرآن والعموم أولى

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf understands wealth and children as worldly life generally, since they are its most coveted parts, citing the verse that calls wealth and sons worldly adornment.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالأموال والأولاد الدنيا وعبر بهما عنهما لكونهما أرغب الأشياء منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is directed at the believers, but is attributed to wealth and children as if they themselves distract, because of their strong causal role; this is an attributional or causal figure.
rows.anchor: والمراد بنهي الأموال وما بعدها نهي المخاطبين وإنما وجه إليها للمبالغة لأنها لقوة تسببها للهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning means being occupied with wealth and children; this is more forceful than simply saying “whoever is distracted by them.”
rows.anchor: أي اللهو بها وهو الشغل وهذا أبلغ مما لو قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are losers because they exchanged enduring, great gain for something fleeting and contemptible; the definite wording, demonstrative, restriction, and repeated attribution intensify the claim.
rows.anchor: حيث باعوا العظيم الباقي بالحقير الفاني وفي التعريف بالأشارة والحصر للخسران فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning prepares for the following general order to spend, countering the hypocrites' call to stop supporting the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وكأنه لما نهى المنافقون عن الإنفاق على من عند رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spend some of the wealth God granted before death approaches, understood as its signs and preliminaries.
rows.anchor: أي بعض ما أعطيناكم وتفضلنا به عليكم من الأموال ادخارا للآخرة من قبل أن يأتي أحدكم الموت أي أماراته ومقدماته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dying person asks for a short extension so that he can give alms.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : ( فيقول رب لو لا أخرتني

rows.speaker: أبي، عبد الله، ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ubayy, ʿAbd Allāh, and Ibn Jubayr read fa-at ṣaddaq, spelling out “so I may give charity.”
rows.anchor: وبذلك قرأ أبي وعبد الله وابن جبير

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي، الزجاج
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and al-Zajjāj parse the jussive wa-akun as coordinated with the syntactic position of fa-aṣṣaddaq: if delayed, I would give charity and be righteous.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب أبو علي الفارسي والزجاج

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl, as reported by Sībawayh, explains the jussive by an implied condition signaled by the wish, though al-Ālūsī likes the analysis but dislikes calling it supposition.
rows.anchor: وحكى سيبويه عن الخليل أنه على توهم الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The difference between coordination to syntactic position and to an imagined condition is verbal: in the former the governor exists but its effect is absent, while in the latter the governor is absent but its effect appears.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين العطف على الموضع والعطف على التوهم أن العامل في العطف على الموضع موجود وأثره مفقود

rows.speaker: الحسن، ابن جبير، أبو رجاء، ابن أبي إسحاق، مالك بن دينار، الأعمش، ابن محيصن، عبد الله بن الحسن، أبو عمرو
rows.claim: These authorities read wa-akūna in the subjunctive, an unproblematic reading after the wish.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وابن جبير وأبو رجاء وابن أبي إسحاق ومالك بن دينار

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr reads wa-akūnu in the indicative; grammarians explain it as a new nominal clause with an omitted subject, though the author questions that rationale.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير ( وأكون ) بالرفع على الاستئناف

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the spending commanded means zakāt and expenditures for pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك أنه قال في قوله تعالى : ( وأنفقوا مما رزقناكم )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes “give alms” as paying zakāt and “be among the righteous” as performing ḥajj.
rows.anchor: فأصدق ) أزكى ( وأكن من الصالحين ) أحج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through al-Tirmidhī, Ibn Jarīr, and al-Ṭabarānī attributes to the Prophet the statement that one able to perform pilgrimage or owing zakāt who fails will ask to return at death.
rows.anchor: فلم يفعلسأل الرجعة عند الموت فقال له رجل : يا ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A narration in al-Tirmidhī's Aḥkām al-Qurʾān is mawqūf on Ibn ʿAbbās, not raised to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وفي أحكام القرآن رواية الترمذي عنه ذلك موقوفا عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed about someone withholding zakāt and argues that asking for return fits his own claim; al-Ālūsī notes the report is not raised to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: إن الآية نزلت في مانع الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the request for delay means a return to worldly life after death, the phrase “before death comes” needs no omitted word.
rows.anchor: سؤالا للرجعة بمعنى الرجوع إلى الدنيا بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will not give a soul respite once its appointed term arrives; ajal may mean the final lifespan or the span allotted from beginning to end.
rows.anchor: انتهى الزمان الممتد لها من أول العمر إلى آخره

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reads the verb with yāʾ, in third person, matching the preceding verse's third-person style.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر بالياء آخر الحروف ليوافق ما قبله في الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because nafsan is indefinite in a negative context, it has universal force, meaning no person is excepted.
rows.anchor: ونفسا لكونها نكرة في سياق النفي

rows.speaker: الكيا
rows.claim: Al-Kiyā uses the command to spend as evidence that zakāt must be paid immediately, without delay.
rows.anchor: واستدل الكيا بقوله تعالى : ( وأنفقوا ) الخ على وجوب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the warning against neglecting these obligations is severe because death may arrive at any time, requiring constant care.
rows.anchor: ونسب للزمخشري أنه قال : ليس في الزجر عن التفريط

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that the commands to spend, the wish for a reprieve, and God's refusal to delay refute determinism; al-Ālūsī answers that the commands do not prove freedom, the wish is no evidence, and the reply merely frustrates the wish.
rows.anchor: وقد أبطل الله تعالى قول المجبرة من جهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the determinist debate is irrelevant to the orthodox, and none of the cited statements proves the point claimed.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن أهل الحق لا يقولون بالجبر فالبحث ساقط عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The day He gathers you” functions adverbially with the statement that you will be informed of your deeds.
rows.anchor: يوم يجمعكم ( ظرف ( لتنبؤن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that resurrection is easy for God confirms His power to raise the dead; the following call to believe renews the passage's appeal to believe in God, the Book, and its messenger.
rows.anchor: فالأول يحقق القدرة على البعث والثاني يؤكد ما سيق له الكلام من الحث على الإيمان به وبما تضمنه من الكتاب وبمن جاء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to believe is really the consequence of the earlier promise that people will be raised and informed, though it is advanced for emphasis and functions parenthetically.
rows.anchor: فالأول يحقق القدرة على البعث والثاني يؤكد ما سيق له الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement that God knows what people do is a parenthesis within the preceding parenthesis and continues the exhortation, like saying, “act, for I am not unaware of you.”
rows.anchor: اعتراض في اعتراض لأنه من تتمة الحث على الإيمان

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī treats the phrase as an adverb modifying khabīr; other authorities take khabīr to imply recompense, including both promise and threat.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي : ظرف لخبير وهو عند غير واحد من الأجلة بمعنى مجازيكم
